title: The futur simple
tagline: Predictions, promises and plans: I will do, I will be, I will have.
goal: Form the futur simple of regular and irregular verbs, use it after quand and si, and know when to prefer it to the near future.

blocks.text: English adds a word («will»). French adds an **ending to the infinitive**, so «will» is built into the verb. The endings look like the present of *avoir*.

notes: -re verbs drop their e: prendr-, écrir-, boir-.

blocks.text: There's always an **r** before the ending: it's the sign of the future. *je parle{r}ai, nous fini{r}ons*.
The endings never change; only the stem does. These are the ones you'll use every day:

blocks.title: One phrase to remember them
blocks.text: *On {verr}a !* (We'll see!) is one of the most useful phrases in French.
The near future [[9]] (*je vais partir*) is «I'm going to leave». The futur simple (*je partirai*) is «I will leave». As in English, both often work.

blocks.title: The big trap: when + future
blocks.text: English says «when I **am** older» (present). French uses the **future**: *Quand je {serai} grand, je serai pilote.*

items.tr: I'll write to you when I have time.

blocks.text: With *si* (if) it works like English: **si + present → future**.
Si + present, future · S'il {pleut}, je {resterai} à la maison.
Never the future after *si* meaning «if»: «si il pleuvra» is wrong, just as «if it will rain» is.

exercises.title: Regular verbs
exercises.instructions: Write the verb in the futur simple.

exercises.title: Irregular verbs
exercises.instructions: Write the verb in the futur simple. Watch the stem.

exercises.title: From near future to futur simple
exercises.instructions: Say the same thing with the futur simple.

items.prompt: Je vais finir ce soir. → Je ___ ce soir.
Ils vont être contents. → Ils ___ contents.
Tu vas avoir froid. → Tu ___ froid.
Elle va faire les courses. → Elle ___ les courses.
On va aller à la plage. → On ___ à la plage.
Je t'appellerai quand j'___ à Paris.
S'il ___ demain, on restera à la maison.
Quand nous ___ le temps, nous voyagerons.
Si j'ai de l'argent, j'___ une voiture.

exercises.title: Say it in French
exercises.instructions: Translate the sentence with the futur simple.

items.prompt: When I'm older, I'll be a doctor.
items.answer: Quand je serai grand, je serai médecin.
accept: Quand je serai grande, je serai médecin.

items.prompt: If you have time, will you come? (tu)
items.answer: Si tu as le temps, tu viendras ?

items.prompt: They will be able to come.

checklist: I form the futur simple with the infinitive and the endings *-ai, -as, -a, -ons, -ez, -ont*.
I know the stems *ser-, aur-, ir-, fer-, viendr-, pourr-, verr-*.
I use the future after *quand* and the present after *si*.
I choose between the near future and the futur simple.

challenge.title: Your life in ten years
challenge.text: Write six predictions about your life in ten years, with at least three irregular verbs and one sentence with *quand*: *Dans dix ans, j'habiterai au bord de la mer. J'aurai un chien. Quand je serai à la retraite, je voyagerai.*
